**Copying many small files into a drive is about 4 times faster.**

## Downloads

| Platform | File | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 (x64) | `cloak-v0.6.8-windows-x64.zip` | [WinFsp](https://winfsp.dev) (`winget install WinFsp.WinFsp`) |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `cloak-v0.6.8-macos-arm64.dmg` | [macFUSE](https://macfuse.github.io) |

**Windows:** unzip and run `Cloak\Cloak.exe`. Keep the folder together: the
engine is in `Cloak\bin`, and your drive list and settings are kept in
`Cloak\cloak-data`.

**macOS:** open the disk image and drag **Cloak** onto **Applications**. The
app isn't notarized, so before opening it the first time, clear the download
quarantine: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Cloak.app` (or
right-click Cloak → Open, then Open again). macFUSE's kernel extension must be
allowed; on Apple Silicon that means its one-time Reduced Security setup.

## Faster

- **Copying small files into a drive** (Explorer, or any program using
  Windows' copy) is about 4 times faster. In a test, 5,000 files of 16 KiB
  took 9.8 s, down from 40 s. Each copied file used to be re-encrypted and
  synced to the disk several times as it was written; a new file doesn't
  need that.

## Known limitations

- **Small files are still slower than on a plain folder** (9.8 s against
  2.3 s in that test). Most of the difference is Windows Defender, which
  makes each file wait at close while it scans it on a drive like this
  one. Large files copy at close to normal speed.
- Auto-lock runs on sleep, not when the screen locks.
- The app isn't code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run
  (More info → Run anyway).
- The middle of every file stays plaintext on disk by design.
- Hidden files of the same drive can be shown to belong together (they share
  the lock's salt); a file on its own looks random.
